name: EPDS
seoDesc: EPDS: answer 11 values and the page computes the result when you press Calculate — formula and worked example included.
summary: The EPDS calculator is a free, no-sign-up health tool. Fill in the 10 fields it asks for and it works out EPDS score straight away, with the formula shown underneath. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the EPDS calculator work?
sections.html:
The EPDS calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports EPDS score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things., the I have looked forward with enjoyment to things. and the I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong.).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

10 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the EPDS calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

EPDS score=(I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things. + the thought of harming myself has occurred to me. + I have looked forward with enjoyment to things. + I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong. + I have been anxious or worried for no good reason. + I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason. + things have been getting on top of me. + I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping. + I have felt sad or miserable. + I have been so unhappy that I have been crying.)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
The form opens with a complete set of values: I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things. set to As much as I always could, I have looked forward with enjoyment to things. set to As much as I ever did, I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong. set to Yes, most of the time and I have been anxious or worried for no good reason. set to No, not at all. Straight away the calculator returns EPDS score = 21.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: EPDS score = 21 should be roughly the size you expected from I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things. set to As much as I always could and I have looked forward with enjoyment to things. set to As much as I ever did.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The EPDS calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the EPDS calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns EPDS score. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the EPDS calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 10 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (10 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports EPDS score = 21. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the EPDS calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
